title: web: Refactor Web Editor using iframes
body:
## What problem(s) does this PR solve?

- Closes #71007
- Closes #57429
- Closes #45799
- Partially address #105060 (it is now possible to "terminate" an instance by double-clicking the `X` close button).

## Additional information

This PR refactors the web editor html shell to run instances inside iframes[1] controlled via message ports.

This, beside fixing few annoying sizing bugs in the page, let us "terminate" a session (game or editor) by removing the iframe from the DOM, thus causing any reasonable browser to garbage collect any stray resource from that instance.


https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2fda73d2-b0a5-4db9-be24-eed62b4661c0


I have removed the "Loader" tab header[2] (see #123149 and godotengine/godot-proposals#15143), but left it as welcome screen and when quitting the editor.

When the user presses `X`, the regular `request_quit` is sent, while if the user double-clicks (rage-detector) they are prompted to confirm if they wish to forcibly terminate the instance.

The PR also adds the `pid` config option and the `onTerminatePID` callback to provide `OS.get_process_id` and `OS.kill` (which are used by the editor to control termination of the running instance).

Fixes `onExecute` to match `OS.execute` signature. I.e. take string `path` as first argument, and (can) return a "Process ID" (this is the breaking change, so probably worth mentioning, but it's easy to work-around on the JS-side).

Some notes
---

[1]
---

In theory, we would not need the `godot.editor.iframe.html` file, and we could use [`srcdoc`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/HTMLIFrameElement/srcdoc), or even better an [empty iframe](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Reference/Elements/iframe#src).

In practice... this does not work well in [chrom*](https://issues.chromium.org/issues/41411856), and while https://github.com/w3c/ServiceWorker/issues/765 correctly mentions it works in Firefox, the Cache is bugged there, and goes to a separete "srcdoc" "subdomain" (resulting in extra downlaods).

Given the original report is only 11 years old, I expect this feature to be fully supported somewhere around 2035.

[2]
---

I have also removed the "Preload ZIP" text as that should be addressed via the PM changes from #123149 (to test this PR you can drop the zip in the PM).

[3]
---

I have added some JSDocs for the `EngineIFrame` class (so it can be added to the HTML reference page), because I think this could be offered as an option in export templates after some stabilization, and once the API gets more stable (would need to move more of the "controller" from `editor.html` to `iframe.js` and generalize it).

I've not added the file to the generation though, as that would only be clutter until it's available in all builds.
